title: ～向け — intended for ～, aimed at ～
summary: Shows that something is made for a particular person or group. It attaches to nouns and appears as ～向けの＋noun or ～向けに＋verb.

body.p: As in 子ども向けの番組 and 海外向けの商品, it names the people or market that the thing targets. It looks from the maker or seller's side: who it was made for.
向け is the intention of the maker (aimed at), while 向き is a natural fit (suited to). 初心者向けの本 is a book made for beginners; 初心者向きの本 is a book that suits beginners.

examples.ja: これは子（こ）ども向（む）けの番組（ばんぐみ）です。
examples.romaji: Kore wa kodomo muke no bangumi desu.
examples.tr: This is a program intended for children.

examples.ja: この雑誌（ざっし）は若（わか）い女性（じょせい）向（む）けに作（つく）られている。
examples.romaji: Kono zasshi wa wakai josei muke ni tsukurarete iru.
examples.tr: This magazine is made for young women.

examples.ja: 海外（かいがい）向（む）けの商品（しょうひん）が、よく売（う）れている。
examples.romaji: Kaigai muke no shōhin ga, yoku urete iru.
examples.tr: Products aimed at overseas markets are selling well.

pitfalls: Do not confuse 向け and 向き: intention is 向け, fitness is 向き.
Use 向けの before a noun and 向けに before a verb.
